deities: Panam Ningthou (Ibudhou Panam Ningthou) - rain and weather god of the Meitei people, protector of crops (especially rice) from hailstorms and thunder, one of the Umang Lai deities
Leimaren Sanarik Chaning Khombi - consort of Panam Ningthou
festivals: Chakpa Haraoba (Lai Haraoba) - annual nine-day festival in the Meitei lunar month of Lamta (March-April), starting from the first Sunday of Lamta; during it no outsiders may stay in the village, and converts away from Sanamahism are not permitted to participate (per tradition)

history.dynasty: Pre-Christian antiquity by tradition; no documented founder dynasty (verify)
history.period: Ancient/traditional - claimed to date to the time of Poireiton of the Khuman clan, the legendary figure who introduced fire to the Meiteis
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: the Temple of Panam Ningthou is the Chakpa Panam Ningthou Meithoupirol Shanglen (also called Mei Mutaba, 'the burning fire') at Andro village, Imphal East district, Manipur - a traditional Sanamahi (Meitei indigenous religion) shrine, NOT a conventional Hindu temple. It is the cult centre of Panam Ningthou, the rain/weather god worshipped principally by the Loi people of Andro, and houses a sacred fire that locals say has been kept burning continuously since it was lit by Poireiton, the King of the Khuman clan. Sources disagree on the date: ~34 BC-18 BC (Wikipedia) vs the 1st century AD (The Better India) - flagged as a date conflict; both agree the fire is believed to be one of India's oldest continuously kept man-made fires. The temple also serves as the Loishang (office) for representatives of the panas (state divisions), with sanctum spaces for Panam Ningthou (right corner) and his consort Leimaren Sanarik Chaning Khombi (left corner), dormitories for boys and girls, and sacred items kept inside. The annual Chakpa Haraoba honours the deity with dance, music, meat and wine. FLAGS: (1) founding-date conflict 34 BC vs 1st century AD - verify; (2) CSV 'state' column held the town name (Andro) - real state is Manipur; (3) coordinates are Andro-village level (24.749, 94.04346), with a temple-specific listing giving 24.750509, 94.045589 nearby - minor discrepancy, verify on the ground; (4) 'closed Sundays' reported by one travel guide only - verify.

name: Panam Ningthou Temple, Andro
town_description: Andro is an ancient village and nagar panchayat in Imphal East district, Manipur, about 25 km east of Imphal in the foothills of the Nongmaiching range. It is earmarked as a Scheduled Caste village and is renowned as a heritage destination: the home of the Loi people (among Manipur's earliest settlers), famous for its unique Charai Taba coil pottery made by married women, the Mutua Museum cultural complex, the Santhei Natural Park, and the ancient Panam Ningthou shrine with its ever-burning sacred fire.
